# ESConv train contexts

## Dialogue 000001

seeker: Hello good afternoon.
supporter: Hi, good afternoon.
seeker: I'm feeling anxious that I am going to lose my job.
supporter: Losing a job is always anxious.
seeker: I hope I don't.
supporter: Why do you think you will lose your job?
seeker: I am on short term disability and I am not ready to go back to work yet but I do not have any job protection.
supporter: Oh so your job is not protected and your short term disability will end soon? Is that correct?
seeker: It's not ending yet, but no my job is not protected. I live in the United States, but I have not been at my job long enough to earn protection for medical leave.
seeker: you have to have been here for a year, and I started November 2020
seeker: I'm afraid that I will lose my job since I'm still on disability for the foreseeable future.
supporter: I see. Have you spoken to HR?
seeker: I have, but they are telling me that it is up to my department manager who isn't actually getting back to me about it yet.
supporter: Your department manager is not answering you?
seeker: No, I have sent them a few emails about it. It makes me nervous. I do not have a phone number to call and my psychiatrist really does not think I am ready to go back to the stress of my job.
seeker: I wish I could just call him, but I do not have a phone number for him. Just his email.
supporter: Have you tried mentioning that to HR?
seeker: HR is the one who gave me his email.
seeker: I don't think he has a direct work line, and they're not allowed to give out personal information.
supporter: Yes that is how most employments work about providing personal information.
supporter: That in itself causes anxiety to most since other forms of communication is not possible especially if they are not responding to ciritcal matters.
seeker: Yes! 100%. Every time my phone rings I get nervous that I'm being fired and I'm worried I made a mistake going out on disability. I needed to though, but I'm nervous.
supporter: No you should not have to feel you made a mistake for the time you are taking out of work for a necessity.
seeker: Thank you for saying that. That does make me feel better. It sucks sometimes we have to choose between our health and our jobs. We don't get paid to take care of our health though, we only get paid to work.
supporter: You know yourself more than anybody and you need to take care of yourself.

## Dialogue 000005

seeker: Hi can you help me with my problem?
supporter: Hello. What's on your mind?
seeker: I'm disgusted with my friend for cheating on her boyfriend. Am I right to feel this way?
supporter: Your feelings are valid, no matter what they are.
supporter: Why do you think you're disgusted with her?
seeker: Because she's not acting the way she should be acting.
seeker: Her boyfriend is a nice guy so he doesn't deserve this treatment
supporter: It sounds like she did something you find really immoral.
supporter: Is their relationship generally pretty good, to your knowledge?
seeker: Yeah, but I'm also thinking it's not my business. I should just stay out of it.
seeker: Well I thought it was good until that happened. He doesn't know. So I just feel gross around them.
supporter: Have you talked to your friend about what she did?
seeker: Yeah, she doesn't really care because she's not going to tell him. I'm questioning whether I should still be friends with her.
supporter: You're definite right to be questioning if this is the sort of person you want to be friends with.
seeker: It's hard to stop thought because we work at the same place.
seeker: though..
supporter: If her behavior is getting to you like this, I definitely suggest you try to keep some distance from her as much as you can.
seeker: Yeah, I've been trying to, but she's always talking to me
supporter: It might be a good idea to explain why you're upset with her, even though that's likely to upset her.
seeker: I guess, but I'd rather just avoid her.
seeker: I'm thinking if I ignore her then she
seeker: she'll get the hint
supporter: I can definitely understand wanting to avoid a confrontation.
seeker: Yeah, I realize she's quite selfish so confronting her wouldn't help.
supporter: What do you think you can do to minimize your contact with her?
seeker: Just not respond to her messages and avoid the areas she's in
supporter: That sounds like a good plan.
seeker: Is that ghosting?
supporter: What one person calls ghosting, someone else can call looking out for yourself.
supporter: It sounds like she knows why you're upset with her and would be able to understand why you're choosing not to talk to her.
supporter: If she's not interested in listening to you or thinking about what she's done, then you need to be doing what is best for you in cutting her out.
